brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 1 base only: piece:0,0,0;half-n (counts piece:1). No other bases placed.

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: No neighboring bases at level 0 and no level 1 bases; build has only piece:0,0,0;half-n and its drawer. Verified by get_build counts.

Configurator allows maximum 1 drawer per half-base on its cut face. find_sockets drawer returns 1 offer for a half base (s13/s15) and 0 after it is filled, and 0 for a full base. Notch/bay drawers require 2-3 touching bases. Build has drawer:0#0,0#cut (1/5). Four additional drawers refused by rule: no socket offers exist.

finish.summary: Single half-n base with 1 drawer placed - the maximum the configurator permits for one base. Verified with find_sockets: only one drawer socket per half base, zero for a full base. Nothing added beside or on top. Five drawers impossible without adding extra bases beside or on top, which violates the brief and has no socket offers.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
